breakfast.name: Kaya Toast (Singaporean Coconut Jam Toast)
breakfast.description: Classic Singaporean breakfast of toast with silky coconut egg jam (kaya) and cold salted butter, traditionally served with half-boiled eggs and black coffee or tea
instructions: Make kaya toast: Toast bread slices in toaster or over charcoal until golden brown
Using serrated knife, carefully split each toasted slice in half horizontally
Expose steamy interior
Smear approximately 1.5 tbsp kaya generously on one half of toast
Top with slab of cold salted butter
Close sandwich with other toast half
Cut diagonally in half
Serve immediately
Make half-boiled eggs: Bring water to rolling boil in pot
Carefully place eggs in boiling water
Cook for 6-7 minutes to achieve soft-boiled eggs with runny yolks
Transfer immediately to ice bath to stop cooking
Gently tap and peel eggs
Place in small bowl or egg cup
Season with soy sauce and white pepper
Serve alongside kaya toast with black coffee or tea
Soft yolk can be mixed with seasonings and eaten with spoon
Toast pieces can be dipped into egg yolk
breakfast.notes: Kaya is custard-like spread made from coconut milk, eggs, sugar, and pandan leaves. Can substitute with homemade kaya or store-bought versions
breakfast.fun_fact: Kaya toast is classic Singaporean breakfast found in every kopi tiam (coffee house). The traditional serving includes half-boiled eggs and black coffee (Kopi-O)

stepHelp: Traditionally toasted over charcoal for a smoky edge, but a regular toaster on medium-high works fine — you want deep golden color, not just warm bread.
Don't be shy — kaya toast is meant to be generously filled, closer to a spread than a thin layer.
Keep the butter cold and in a slab rather than softened — it melts slowly into the hot toast for pockets of richness instead of disappearing completely.
Lower them in gently with a spoon rather than dropping them, so the shells don't crack.
6 minutes gives a very runny yolk, 7 minutes a slightly firmer but still soft one — timing is the whole game with half-boiled eggs.
This stops the cooking instantly — skip it and the eggs keep cooking from residual heat, overshooting the soft yolk you want.
Half-boiled eggs are delicate — crack the shell gently all over first, then peel, since the white is much softer than a hard-boiled egg.

variations.title: Homemade Kaya
variations.text: Make your own coconut egg jam from coconut milk, eggs, sugar, and pandan leaf for a fresher, more fragrant spread.

variations.title: Different Bread
variations.text: Try it on thick white toast, brioche, or even a baguette for a different texture — traditional kopitiams often use a specific soft white loaf.

variations.title: Jam Instead of Kaya
variations.text: In a pinch, any good fruit jam with cold butter makes a quick, if less traditional, version.

variations.title: Steamed Egg Style
variations.text: Some kopitiams steam the eggs instead of boiling for an even silkier texture.

variations.title: Extra Butter Layer
variations.text: Add a second thin slice of butter for an even richer bite, especially if your bread is on the drier side.

serveWith.intro: A kopitiam (coffee house) breakfast is built around this exact combination — toast, egg, and something to drink.

items.title: Kopi-O (Black Coffee)
items.text: Strong, sweetened black coffee is the traditional kopitiam pairing.

items.title: Teh (Milk Tea)
items.text: A sweet, creamy alternative to coffee if you want something milder.

items.title: Extra Half-Boiled Eggs
items.text: Order or make a second egg on the side — they're the perfect dip for any leftover toast corners.

items.title: Fresh Fruit
items.text: Something light like papaya or melon rounds out the richness of the buttery toast.

items.title: Extra Soy & Pepper
items.text: Keep more on the table for dipping toast directly into the egg.

expertTips.title: Timing the Eggs Is Everything
expertTips.text: Have your water at a full rolling boil before the eggs go in, and start timing immediately — a slow simmer will give you inconsistent results.

expertTips.title: Toast It Twice If Needed
expertTips.text: If your bread isn't crisp enough after one pass, toast it again — you want real crunch to contrast the soft kaya and butter.

expertTips.title: Cold Butter, Hot Toast
expertTips.text: The contrast of cold butter against hot toast is the whole point — don't soften the butter first.

expertTips.title: Season the Egg Simply
expertTips.text: Just soy sauce and white pepper — the egg's richness doesn't need much else.

storage.title: Kaya
storage.text: Store-bought or homemade kaya keeps in the fridge in a sealed jar for up to 2 weeks.

storage.title: Assembled Toast
storage.text: Best eaten immediately — the toast loses its crunch quickly once assembled with the kaya and butter.

storage.title: Eggs
storage.text: Half-boiled eggs don't store well and should be made fresh; they're not meant to be held at room temperature for long due to the soft-cooked yolk.

breakfast.makeAhead: The only truly make-ahead component is the kaya itself — a batch keeps in the fridge for up to 2 weeks, so you can make your own coconut jam once and have kaya toast ready to assemble any morning. The toast and eggs should always be made fresh to order.

faqs.a: Look for it at Asian grocery stores, often in the jam or Southeast Asian foods aisle — or make your own from coconut milk, eggs, sugar, and pandan leaf.

faqs.q: How do I get the egg yolk really runny?
faqs.a: 6 minutes in a full rolling boil, straight into an ice bath, gives the classic very-runny kaya toast egg. Adjust by 30-second increments to find your preference.

faqs.q: Can I make this without a toaster?
faqs.a: Yes — a dry skillet or grill pan over medium heat works, just watch it closely so it toasts evenly without burning.

faqs.q: Is the egg safe to eat half-boiled?
faqs.a: As with any soft-cooked egg, use fresh, properly refrigerated eggs from a reliable source, and eat them freshly made rather than holding them at room temperature.

lunch.name: Laksa (Spiced Noodle Soup)
lunch.description: Popular Singaporean lunch - rich, spiced coconut broth with noodles and seafood or chicken
instructions: Heat 1 tbsp oil in pot, add laksa paste and fry for 2 minutes until fragrant
Add coconut milk and broth, bring to simmer
Cook protein until done, add to soup
Cook rice noodles separately according to package
Divide noodles into bowls
Pour hot laksa broth over noodles
Top with egg, bean sprouts, cilantro, basil and fried tofu
Serve with lime wedge on side
lunch.notes: Laksa paste is essential - can be store-bought or homemade. Coconut milk creates rich, smooth base
lunch.fun_fact: Laksa is popular Singaporean lunch with many regional variations throughout Southeast Asia

dinner.name: Hainanese Chicken Rice (Singapore Version)
dinner.description: Poached chicken with fragrant rice - Singapore's national dish
ingredients: For sauce: 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 1 tablespoon dark soy, 1 tablespoon rice vinegar, 1 clove garlic minced, 1 red chili sliced
For ginger sauce: 100g fresh ginger, minced, 3 tablespoons oil, salt, white pepper
instructions: Bring chicken stock to boil in large pot
Add smashed ginger, garlic, scallions, bay leaves
Carefully place whole chicken into boiling stock
Return to boil, then reduce heat to simmer
Simmer 35-40 minutes until chicken is fully cooked and tender
Remove chicken, reserve cooking liquid (skim fat for rice cooking)
Measure 750ml reserved chicken stock
Heat chicken fat or oil in saucepan over medium heat
Add minced garlic and ginger, stir-fry 2 minutes until fragrant
Add jasmine rice, stir constantly for 2 minutes until each grain is coated
Add reserved chicken stock and salt
Bring to boil, then reduce heat to low
Cover and cook 18-20 minutes until rice is fluffy
Let rest 5 minutes covered
Meanwhile, prepare soy-based sauce by combining ingredients
Prepare ginger sauce: mix minced ginger with hot oil, add salt and white pepper
Cut cooked chicken into serving pieces
Arrange rice on platter with chicken pieces on top
Garnish with cucumber slices and cilantro
Serve with both sauces on the side
dinner.notes: Cooking rice in chicken fat is essential for authentic flavor. Chicken must be fully submerged
dinner.fun_fact: Hainanese Chicken Rice originated from Hainan province China but perfected and popularized by Singapore
alternatives: Use chicken parts instead of whole bird
